correctness.rationale: The Fano-incidence presentation reconstructs the 14-vertex, 21-edge Heawood graph. Exhaustive enumeration gives 3,461 nonempty matchings with face vector (21,168,644,1218,1050,336,24). The deterministic element matching has 1,722 cover pairs, one critical 0-cell and sixteen critical 4-cells. The complete 14,574-edge oriented Hasse diagram is acyclic by exhaustive topological sort. Forman discrete Morse theory therefore gives a CW model with one 0-cell and sixteen 4-cells, hence a wedge of sixteen 4-spheres. Independent mod-2 boundary ranks give reduced Betti number 16 only in degree 4.

evidence: Matsushita arXiv:1910.00186 defines matching complexes and proves wedge decompositions for polygonal line tilings; its full text has no “Heawood”, “Fano”, or “toroid” occurrence.
Bayer--Jelić Milutinović--Vega 2023 define their extended polygonal line tilings as strings of cycles with prescribed overlaps; their theorem establishes a wedge-of-spheres form for that family.
The Heawood graph is nonplanar and is the Fano-plane Levi graph, so it is outside those chain-of-cycles families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest family theorems guarantee wedge behavior only for structurally different graph classes and neither fixes the sphere dimension or multiplicity for the Heawood graph.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical highly symmetric cubic graph and Fano-plane incidence object. Exact matching-complex homotopy types are available only for selected classes, making this graph-specific benchmark mathematically motivated. The finite certificate compresses 3,461 faces to one critical vertex and sixteen critical 4-cells, giving a reusable exact test case for topological-combinatorics computations.
